discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that when two graphene sheets are twisted to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees, the electronic bands become almost flat, so that interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this, finding correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The phase diagram closely resembles that of the cuprates, including strange-metal transport. The work founded 'twistronics', a platform in which the twist angle, gating and screening tune the strength of electron correlations continuously and cleanly. Moire materials have since shown correlated Chern insulators, orbital magnetism and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect at zero magnetic field. This combination of an elegant theoretical prediction with a decisive experimental discovery lets us study, in one controllable system, the physics of entangled quantum matter without quasiparticles.
